newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-DUBLIN FLYER HEADS GRAND NATIONAL WEIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DUBLIN FLYER HEADS GRAND NATIONAL WEIGHTS.

text.p: Dublin Flyer, a bold-jumping front-runner, heads the weights published on Tuesday for the Grand National steeplechase to be run at Aintree on April 5.
Dublin Flyer, a leading fancy for next month's Cheltenham Gold Cup, is trained by veteran Tim Forster who has won the National three times since 1972.
Organisers have altered the weight structure this year, giving the top weight more to carry, and hope the race will attract more runners than last year's field of 27, the smallest for 36 years.
The 1996 winner Rough Quest is injured and misses this year's race.
Another Cheltenham Gold Cup runner, Coome Hill, trained near the Cornish coast, is thought to be favourably treated with 22lbs (10 kgs) less to carry than Dublin Flyer.
But bookmakers installed proven stayer Lo Stregone as 14-1 favourite with Coome Hill and Dublin Flyer at 16-1 along with Encore Un Peu, second in last year's National.
